tag: Schools, workplaces & study — always in use
bandTip: 🎯 Coherence: notice that the exact same sentence frames ("I enjoy it because...", "I don't mind + -ing, but...") work whether you're a pupil, a student, or a working professional — learn the frame once, then just plug in whatever's true for you.

questions.text: Are you a student? What school do you go to?

topStructures.note: These are the ones I'd actually want students to learn and reuse, rather than memorise dozens of expressions:

items.example: It's best known for its historic architecture.

items.pattern: I'd say the biggest difference is...
items.example: I'd say the biggest difference is the pace of life.
I could see myself living in the countryside one day.
I like the idea of living somewhere quieter.

items.pattern: X tends to be..., whereas Y...
items.example: City life tends to be busier, whereas the countryside is much quieter.

items.pattern: There are more... than there used to be
items.example: There are more modern buildings than there used to be.
I've never actually lived in the countryside.
Even though I live elsewhere now, I still feel connected to my hometown.
I go back whenever I get the chance.
I find the countryside relaxing because there's less noise.

topStructures.closingNote: These are much more valuable for an 8+ student than memorising a long list of "advanced" hometown vocabulary. They give the student structures they can actually recycle naturally across dozens of Part 1 topics.

questions.text: Please describe your hometown a little.

It's probably best known for its historic buildings and traditional architecture, and there are quite a few places that date back hundreds of years. At the same time, it's a fairly quiet place, so life there is a lot slower-paced than in a big city.

theme: A Place You'd Like to Visit in Your Free Time
cueCardPoints: how long you will stay there
why you'd like to visit it
howToBuildTips: Don't answer the bullet points one by one — connect them into a natural story instead of a mechanical list (Situation → Place → Activities → Time → Reason → Feeling).
Open with your personal situation first: "To be honest, + situation. So, if I had the chance, I'd probably..." — this sounds spontaneous, not memorised.
Build activity chains instead of naming one activity: "We'd probably..., then..., and after that..." — this helps you speak for the full 2 minutes without repeating yourself.
Don't force idioms into the answer — using two or three naturally beats cramming in five just to show off vocabulary.

models.text:
To be honest, I barely have any free time these days. I work quite a lot, and I even work at the weekends, so I have to make a real effort to carve out some time for myself. I don't have one particular place that I always go to, but if I had a completely free day, I'd love to head out to the mountains with a few close friends.

The mountains aren't too far from my city, so we'd probably set off early in the morning and spend the whole day there. We wouldn't make any complicated plans. We'd probably go for a long hike, take some photos, have a picnic, and just take in the scenery. We might also find a quiet spot and sit around and catch up because we don't get to see each other very often.

I'd probably stay there from morning until late afternoon, or even until sunset if we weren't too tired. I think a full day would be enough to get away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life without making the trip too exhausting.

The main reason I'd like to go is that my routine can get pretty repetitive. I'm constantly working, studying or dealing with one thing or another, so sometimes I feel like I need to hit the reset button. Being out in nature would help me clear my head, let off some steam, and simply enjoy being around people I care about.

So, for me, it's not really about finding some amazing tourist destination. It's about getting away from it all, slowing down for a while, and feeling alive again. That's probably what I'd value most in my free time.

I'd say I barely have any free time these days, because I even work at the weekends, so finding time to relax can be a bit of a challenge. That said, I do try to spare some time for myself whenever I get the chance. I don't really have one specific place in mind, though. I usually prefer spending my free time with a few close friends, and we're pretty flexible about where we go.

For example, sometimes we head to a park and just sit around, have a chat, and catch up on what's been going on in our lives. We might grab something to eat or drink and simply take it easy for a couple of hours. At other times, we stay indoors and play computer games together. It's nothing special, but it helps me switch off after a long and tiring week.

However, if I had a whole day free, I'd probably head out to the mountains with my friends. I'd love to go for a hike, enjoy the fresh air, take in the scenery, and just get away from it all. We'd probably stay there for the whole day, maybe from early morning until sunset. I think that would be enough time to clear my head without having to rush back.

The main reason I'd like to visit a place like this is that I sometimes feel like I'm stuck in the same routine. I really want to feel alive, forget about work for a while, and relieve some of the stress that builds up during the week. For me, it's less about the actual place and more about having a chance to breathe, recharge, and enjoy the moment.
